title.en: Matching solids with everyday objects (additional, not in the textbook)

text.en: Look around the classroom. The duster is a cuboid, the chalk is a cylinder, a dice is a cube and a ball is a sphere.

Match the solid shapes with everyday objects. A brick, a matchbox and a book are cuboids.
A dice and a sugar cube are cubes. A can, a pipe and a candle are cylinders.
A joker's cap, an ice cream cone and a funnel are cones. A ball and a marble are spheres.
Some objects are made of more than one shape. A rocket has a cone, cylinders and a cuboid.
The textbook asks: which shapes have no edges, only flat faces, only curved faces, or both flat and curved faces?
A sphere has no edge. A cube and cuboid have only flat faces. A cylinder and cone have both flat and curved faces.
(additional, not in the textbook) Name the odd shape out in a group by saying which one rolls and which one only slides.

problem.en: Name the shape of a can of juice and say what faces it has.

why.en: It has two circles and a tube.

text.en: It has two flat faces on top and bottom.
It has one curved face around the side.

prompt.en: A friend says all solid shapes can roll. Is that right?

requiredIdeas.en: A cylinder rolls on its curved side

points.en: Everyday objects look like solid shapes.
Some shapes have flat faces, some curved, some both.
